taxonomic_note: Kew accepts Yucca rupicola; native range is south-central Texas (southeastern Edwards Plateau) to northeastern Mexico. FNA describes it as endemic to the southeastern Edwards Plateau within its U.S. range.
look_here_first: Look at the leaves before the flower: a low, essentially trunkless colony with flexible dark-green leaves that twist helically and have wavy/denticulate orange to reddish-brown margins.
project_tracker_diagnostic: acaulescent/trunkless open colonies of 2–15 rosettes; flexible lanceolate leaves, 35–60 cm long and 1.7–4 cm wide; leaves conspicuously twisted and strongly concave; leaf margins wavy or minutely toothed, dark orange to reddish brown; inflorescence rises well beyond the rosette; fruit erect, dry, dehiscent capsule rather than a fleshy berry

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — UT Plant Resources Center Flora of Purola Preserve lists Yucca rupicola among naturally occurring, non-introduced plants of northern Hays County. Travis — Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list for Travis County includes twist-leaf yucca (Yucca rupicola). Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed Vascular Plants of Williamson County treatment for Yucca rupicola.

morphology_keys.joey_field_note: Joey's landscaping frame gives a clear whole-rosette view and leaf architecture. Use the low basal rosette and visibly twisting blades as the immediate field gestalt, then confirm the orange-to-reddish wavy/denticulate margins.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Yucca constricta: Both are low colony-forming yuccas, but Y. rupicola has broader flexible twisted leaves with orange/red wavy-toothed margins; Y. constricta has much narrower mostly straight leaves with whitish filiferous margins and a deeply waist-constricted capsule. Yucca pallida: Pale yucca is usually glaucous blue-green with straighter leaves and flatter yellowish margins; Y. rupicola is darker green, visibly twisted, and has wavy orange/red margins.
